The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ for the damages sustained to the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53C3135 in the road traffic accident occurred on 17.06.2019.

2. It is the case of petitioner that, on 17.06.2019 at about 11.50. p.m., the empty lorry bearing registration No.KA53 C3135 was proceeding towards Thoralakki Village from Tekal, near Shettihalli Village, TekalThoralakki Road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, at that time another Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53C3049 came from opposite direction at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner tipper lorry bearing reg. No. KA53C 3135 and due to impact the Lorry extensively damaged beyond repairable.
Further petitioner M.V.C.No.7102/2019 4 SCCH  7 SCCHsss SCCH - 7SCC contended his lorry was of 2016 year model and same was road worthy condition valued at Rs.25,00,000/.

After completion of the formalities he got released the lorry from Masti Police Station and lorry was toed to Trident Trucking, Sales and Service which is authorized dealers of Bharath Benz Commercial Vehicles at,
Boodihal, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore Rural for repairs.
The experts estimated the damages at Rs.18,02,165/ including the laobur charges.
The petitioner contended that he was earning Rs.1,00,000/ per month by using the tipper lorry by transporting the stone products i.e., jelly and M.Sand.

3. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 is placed exparte and the respondent No.2 has appeared through their counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 insurer denied the entire contentions of the petitioner.

Further contended that they have issued the policy to the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA 53C3049 and as on the date of the accident the policy was in force and their liability is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy, as such they are not liable to pay M.V.C.No.7102/2019 6 SCCH  7 SCCHsss SCCH - 7SCC any compensation to the petitioners.
Hence they prayed to dismiss the petition.

(2) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

Issue No.1: In support of the case of the petitioner the GPA holder of the petitioner got examined as PW.1 and in his examination in chief he deposed as per the contentions taken by him and got marked authorization letter as per Ex.P1, FIR as per Ex.P2, Complaint as per Ex.P3, Spot mahazar as per Ex.P4, IMV report as per Ex.P5 and Charge sheet as per Ex.P6.
By perusing these documents they goes to shows that this accident was took place due to the negligence of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53C3049.
Further in the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worth is brought on record to show that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53C3049.

Further by perusing the Charge Sheet marked as per Ex.P.6 it clearly goes to shows that the Investigating M.V.C.No.7102/2019 9 SCCH  7 SCCHsss SCCH - 7SCC Officer after conducting investigation came to the conclusion that this accident was took place due to the negligence of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53C3049.
Further by perusing the IMV Report marked as per Ex.P.5 it goes to shows that in this accident Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53 C3135 was sustained damages.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 partly in the affirmative.

Further he deposed that the owner of the tipper and insurer of the Tipper lorry were not permitted them to repair the vehicle only after dis metaling the vehicle they will came to know about the actual damages to the vehicle and they can tell what is the approximate amount for repair of the said vehicle.
He denied that as per IMV report the front portion and light of the Tipper lorry only damaged in this accident.

From the evidence of PW.2 it is clear that they examined the vehicle and after examination they have prepared the approximate amount for repair of the Tipper lorry and as per their estimation Rs.17,12,165/ is require for repair the vehicle and for repair the vehicle the service charges is Rs.90,000/.

The PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner has not furnished the documents sought by them as such the insurer of the damaged Tipper lorry was not made any M.V.C.No.7102/2019 17 SCCH  7 SCCHsss SCCH - 7SCC survey.
Hence it is clear that the insurer of the petitioner's tipper lorry was not done any survey of the vehicle damaged in this accident.
The Ex.P.21 is the estimation wherein the repair charges is shown at Rs.17,12,165/ and total cost of labour charges is Rs.90,000/ in all Rs.18,02,165/.
It shows that there are chances of repairing the damaged tipper in the service station of PW.2.

The petitioner has contended that in this accident their Tipper lorry vehicle is totally damaged but to show that their tipper vehicle is totally damaged there is no any survey report from the surveyor of the insurance company of the petitioner tipper.

From the evidence of PW.2 nothing worth is brought on record to show that in this accident due to damages caused to the Tipper Lorry the Tipper vehicle is unrepairable as such the petitioner sustained total loss due to the damages caused to their Tipper lorry in this accident.

M.V.C.No.7102/2019 18 SCCH  7 SCCHsss SCCH - 7SCC Hence it is clear that without their being any documentary evidence to show that the Tipper of the petitioner was completely damaged and it is in non repairable condition the contention of the petitioner is not acceptable one.

14. Further the respondent got examined their Official as RW.1 and in his examination in chief he deposed as per contention taken by them and they got marked Authorization letter as per Ex.R.1 and Policy copy as per Ex.R.2.

In his crossexamination he admitted that as on the date of the accident the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53C3049 was insured by them and the driver of the said Tipper lorry was having valid driving licence and the police have filed Charge Sheet against the driver of the said Tipper lorry.

Further he admitted that in this accident another Tipper lorry driver has sustained some small injuries and he deposed that they are not M.V.C.No.7102/2019 19 SCCH  7 SCCHsss SCCH - 7SCC having any documents to show that they have paid compensation to the driver of the Tipper lorry.

From the evidence of RW.1 it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA 53C3049 was insured by them and the driver of the said Tipper lorry was having valid driving licence and Charge Sheet is also on the driver of the said Tipper lorry.

Hence it is clear that the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, but the petitioner has not put forth any acceptable material evidence to show that in this accident their lorry was sustained total loss.

Hence M.V.C.No.7102/2019 20 SCCH  7 SCCHsss SCCH - 7SCC without their being any evidence to show that in this accident the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA53C 3135 was completely damaged the contention of the petitioner that they are entitled for compensation for total loss from the respondents is not acceptable one.
Hence, I answered the issue No.2 in the Negative.
